gen-dafont-bloody-gf-chocolate-classical: Commanding, Bloody pushes its lowercase into plump rounds. Chocolate Classical Sans carries a sizable lowercase and a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never closes up, a modern counterweight to the shouting above.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-cossette-texte: Bloody's plump, rounded lowercase makes every heading feel heavy and loud. Cossette Texte keeps a monoline stroke and wide-eyed lowercase e forms, so this plain sans should glide through pages of text without tiring the eye.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-gafata: Gafata reads contemporary and businesslike, with a deep band of lowercase. Page after page, its wide-eyed e forms keep the text open and easy going, leaving Bloody to do all the shouting.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Loud and plump up top, Bloody sets the mood with its commanding rounded letters. And Hedvig Letters Sans, with its open-mouthed c and lowercase nearly the height of capitals, lets the page settle down.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-heebo: Heebo reads direct and uncluttered, its curves stopping short instead of closing in. Heebo stays quiet while Bloody roars, and that gap in volume is what holds the pairing together.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hind-guntur: Weight first: Bloody's plump, rounded lowercase gives headings a commanding presence. Hind Guntur, plain sans drawn like steel cable with no swelling in the line, makes the difference the whole point.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru keeps every stroke solid, with no hairlines to squint at. Bloody is built to grab attention with its plump rounds, while this sans-serif simply holds its shape at small sizes.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hind-siliguri: Bloody pushes its lowercase into plump, rounded shapes that feel commanding, almost brash, before the text even begins. Hind Siliguri, plain sans with a constant line, rewards a slightly larger size.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara reads clean and spacious, its rounded glyphs open at the ends. Pair Bloody at a generous size with Hind Vadodara in modest text sizes, where its uniform line stays crisp.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-inter-tight: Plump, rounded lowercase is the first thing Bloody gives you, and it lands with a commanding thud. Bloody grabs attention; Inter Tight, sans-serif drawn like fineliner, handles the reading.
